title: The Seafood Palace he cannot remember
summary: The interviewer asks about a 1975 jazz club on 48th Street; Barefield remembers neither the club nor many records he plays on, though he recalls the Jazz Museum.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was the band you had at the Seafood Palace, that thing that didn't last too long? I know they had several different bands in there, but I know you had a band over there.
Yeah, where Gluckstein's used to be on 48th Street. This was about four years ago.
Or something like that it was called. I know you had --
Because I was in Pier 52 with Frankie Dash and --
They tried a jazz club there for a while, and it didn't last too long.
Yeah, I remember seeing the ads and everything, you know. But I guess that's not proof. They might have advertised you and you weren't there. That's possible, though I seem to remember that --
I don't even remember the Seafood Palace.

I think that's what it was called. I'm trying to remember Gluck. (Inaudible), but it used to be Cottstern's Restaurant, which is a kosher restaurant. On that site they put in this place. I remember I went to hear somebody there once, and I can't remember who it was now. Oh, maybe it was Al Porcino had a big band there for one night, but there was a jazz policy for a little while, and then it just kind of faded away.
But I remember you played there and -- or you were advertised. Seafood Playhouse, Seafood -- not palace, summer of '75. You don't remember it?
That's right. I went to (inaudible) Europe with a guy that I was on played about a three hour concert with records, and half of them I didn't --
I knew my playing, but I didn't remember.
Then you also played at the Jazz Museum. Do you remember that?
